summary.intent: Assess Phase 72 readiness, reconcile stale/pending todos across Phases 70-73, then plan/execute/ship Phase 72 while responding to an interrupting CI fire (web-e2e and desktop-e2e failures) and subsequent web-e2e flakiness before resuming Phase 72 planning.
summary.outcome: Retired 8 stale Phase 71 todos and updated ROADMAP scope for 72/73 (staged, uncommitted); root-caused and fixed three real CI regressions (FUSE seq-1 equivocation in PR #601, stale rotation-durability floor-store test in PR #600, sdk-e2e Test 21 idempotency flake) plus a greptile perf nit and four additional web-e2e timing flakes, merged both PRs, and resumed Phase 72 planning through research and pattern-mapping with the planner spawned.

repo: Phase 71 (#599) shipped without retiring its 8 source todos from pending/ — this repo's convention is to delete/move todos to completed/ on ship, and that step was skipped, causing drift

IPNS anti-equivocation gate (Phase 71, ipns.service.ts) rejects same-sequence republish with a different CID (400) — correct behavior, but FUSE's publish_file_node hardcoded seq=1 on first-publish without resolving first, causing legitimate re-key republishes to collide with the gate

Phase 70.1 collapsed two IndexedDB stores (generation-high-water, seq-high-water) into a single rotation-floor store (DB cipherbox-rotation-state v2, keyed by nodeId) but the web-e2e test helper wasn't updated to match

Phase 71 renamed share DTO fields (readDescriptorRef→encryptedReadKey, rootIpnsName→shareRootIpnsName) but a desktop-e2e .mts test driver (shared-scope-exit-rotation.mts) retained the old field names, tripping forbidNonWhitelisted validation

ci-e2e.yml (Web/Desktop E2E) only triggers on push-to-main or workflow_dispatch, never on PRs — so PR-level validation of e2e-touching changes requires manual dispatch via `gh workflow run <file> --ref <branch>` (the `-f ref=` form 422s on this repo's older workflow definition)

web-e2e Playwright config: ciFloor() helper raises wait timeouts to a 60s floor only under CI (process.env.CI); local runs use much tighter waits (15-30s), causing IPNS-gated mutation tests (batch delete/move, restore, multi-delete) to flake locally on a cold/loaded stack even though they pass reliably in CI

webServer.reuseExistingServer in playwright.config.ts is `!process.env.CI`, so setting CI=1 locally to get the 60s ciFloor also disables server reuse and conflicts with an already-running dev stack — must temporarily patch webServer config to reuse if you want a true CI-equivalent local run

GSD hook JSON fragments (plan:pre capIds) contain raw/literal newlines inside string values, making them non-strict JSON — `jq`/direct parsing fails and requires a lenient control-char-escaping parser script

code.finding: publish_file_node's first-publish branch hardcoded seq=1 gated only by 'inode cid empty', causing equivocation-gate rejections on re-key republishes; fixed by resolving IPNS first via resolve_ipns_for_replay and routing Found results into publish_with_cas_retry instead of assuming NotFound

publish_with_cas_retry given optional preresolved_seq param (greptile perf fix) to avoid a redundant second IPNS resolve on the Found path; conflict-retry path still always re-resolves since pre-resolved values go stale after a conflict

readDurableFloors/writeDurableSeqFloor read/wrote the retired generation-high-water/seq-high-water IDB stores; fixed to use the single rotation-floor store with read-modify-write semantics for seq (direct overwrite, not max-preserving)

Test 21 (D-06 concurrent first-publish) asserted exactly one 200 + one 409, but same-CID idempotency (Phase 71) makes two 200s a valid outcome too; rewritten to accept fulfilled.length>=1 and any rejected results must be 409

ciFloor() helper is the source of the local/CI timeout asymmetry — waitForItemToDisappear and similar waiters apply this floor, explaining why several full-workflow.spec.ts tests (4.10, 4.11, 6.6.2, 8.2) pass in CI but flake locally on tight timeouts

workflow: When a background/dispatched CI validation run fails, separate infra-step failures from actual test-step failures before deep-diving (distinguishes real regressions from unrelated infra flakes)

Verify agent-proposed patches against the actual current schema/source/signatures before applying, rather than trusting subagent diagnosis blindly — caught correct patches and validated them independently each time

When two fixes touch the same underlying primitive (a shared CAS/write helper), land them on the same PR/branch rather than splitting, so the branch's own CI run validates the interaction and avoids a merge-order dependency

Local reproduction of CI-only flakes may require replicating the exact timeout regime (CI=1 env) rather than assumed-equivalent local settings, since helper functions like ciFloor() branch explicitly on process.env.CI
Use `gh workflow run <file> --ref <branch>` (not `-f ref=`) to dispatch a workflow against a specific branch when the workflow definition predates a ref input parameter

Before dispatching a validation CI run against a feature branch, check whether it needs rebasing onto main first to include prerequisite merged fixes (e.g., #600 needed #601's FUSE fix for its dispatched desktop-e2e leg to pass)

friction: Repeated whack-a-mole local flakes (4.10, 4.11, 2.1) each blocked reaching the target tests (6.6.2, 8.2) in serial full-workflow.spec.ts runs, requiring multiple ~10-20 min re-run cycles before finally forcing a true CI-equivalent regime (CI=1 + temp reuseExistingServer patch) to get a clean local pass
